problem: A mail carrier delivered parcels to 5 houses before lunch and to 6 more houses after lunch. How many houses did she deliver to in all?
follow_up_questions: Every house got 3 parcels. How many parcels did she deliver?

problem: How many birdhouses did Tomasz paint this weekend? He painted 5 on Saturday, then 6 more on Sunday.
follow_up_questions: Each birdhouse needs 3 nails for its roof. How many nails did the roofs need?

problem: A coach shared 24 tennis balls between two teams, the Lions and the Hawks. The Lions got 15. How many balls did the Hawks get?
follow_up_questions: The Hawks lost 4 of their balls over the fence. How many do they still have?
The Lions lost twice as many balls as the Hawks did. How many balls did the Lions lose?

problem: Grandma Ruth knitted 24 hats and gave 15 of them to Hillside School. The rest went to Brookside School. What number of hats did Brookside School get?
follow_up_questions: Brookside handed out 4 of its hats on the first cold day. How many hats does it have left to hand out?
On that day Hillside handed out twice as many hats as Brookside. How many did Hillside hand out?

problem: A painter can paint 4 fence panels each day. How many days will it take him to paint 36 panels around the park?
Lena reads 4 chapters every evening. Her adventure book has 36 chapters. After how many evenings will she finish the book?
A printer at the school office prints 8 pages every minute. How many pages does it print in 7 minutes?
follow_up_questions: 6 of the pages come out smudged. How many clean pages are there?

problem: For 7 minutes a bottling machine at the juice factory was running, filling 8 bottles each minute. What number of bottles did it fill?
follow_up_questions: A worker removes 6 bottles with loose caps. How many bottles are fine?

problem: Ravi gathered 23 pine cones in the park. He tossed 15 of them into his basket. How many pine cones was he still holding?
follow_up_questions: He put the rest in the basket too, then picked up 7 more. How many pine cones has he gathered in all?
He gives a third of them to his class for an art project. How many pine cones does the class get?

problem: How many library books was Mrs. Osei still carrying? She had collected 23 returned books from the drop box and had already slid 15 of them onto the cart.
follow_up_questions: After placing the rest on the cart, she found 7 more books in the drop box. How many books has she collected now?
A third of all the books need new covers. How many books need covers?

problem: In the craft box there are 12 red crayons and 9 blue crayons. What is the total number of crayons in the box?
follow_up_questions: Each child at the table gets 3 crayons. How many children can get crayons?

problem: How many apples did Mei pack into her picnic basket, if she put in 12 green apples and 9 red ones?
follow_up_questions: The family eats 3 apples every hour. How many hours will the apples last?

problem: Tamar has 24 guests coming to her garden party, and each small table seats 4 guests. How many tables does she need?
follow_up_questions: She already owns 2 tables. How many more tables must she get?
Every new table needs 8 screws to put together. How many screws does she need?
Screws are sold in bags of 10. How many bags must she buy to have enough?

problem: A rabbit hutch fits 4 rabbits. What number of hutches will Mr. Varga need for the 24 rabbits on his farm?
follow_up_questions: 2 hutches are already built. How many more does he need to build?
He uses 8 boards for each new hutch. How many boards does he need?
Boards are sold in bundles of 10. How many bundles must he buy so he has enough?

problem: Ana put 14 photos in her scrapbook in May and 17 in June. How many photos did she add during those two months?
follow_up_questions: She added 9 more in July. How many photos has she added now?
The scrapbook has room for 50 photos. How many places are still empty?

problem: In June, 17 bottle caps went into Tobias's jar, after 14 had gone in during May. What is the total number of caps he put in over those months?
follow_up_questions: July added another 9. What is his total?
The jar holds 50 caps when full. How many more caps fit in it?

problem: Each of the 9 tables in the classroom has 2 chairs. How many chairs are there?
A florist puts 2 roses into every vase. She fills 9 vases for a wedding. Find the number of roses she uses.
A city bus has 7 rows on its top deck, with 4 seats in each row. How many seats are on the top deck?
follow_up_questions: 19 of those seats are taken. How many are free?

problem: Work out how many cupcakes the baker must ice: she has 7 trays, and 4 cupcakes sit on every tray.
follow_up_questions: So far 19 have icing. How many still need it?

problem: Each comic book at the fair costs 3 dollars, and Ines has 21 dollars to spend. How many comic books can she buy? The fair tent is striped red and white.
follow_up_questions: Her friend buys 4 more comic books. How many comic books do the two of them have?
Then 3 of the comics get soaked in the rain. How many are still dry?

problem: Kenta wants to buy seed packets for the school garden. The garden is behind the gym. He has 21 dollars, and one packet costs 3 dollars. What is the greatest number of packets he can buy?
follow_up_questions: His teacher brings 4 more packets. How many packets do they have now?
Birds peck open 3 of the packets. How many packets are left?

problem: A pizza place puts 4 slices on every plate. How many plates does it need for 32 slices?
In groups of 4, the 32 dancers of the school show step onto the stage. What number of groups take the stage?
The school has 13 bikes in the front rack and 15 in the back rack. What is the number of bikes at the school?
follow_up_questions: 4 of the bikes in the back rack are ridden home at lunch. How many bikes are still in the racks?

problem: How many tents are at the campsite? Near the lake there are 13 tents, and 15 more stand under the trees.
follow_up_questions: Strong wind blows down 4 of the tents under the trees. How many tents are still standing?

problem: A gardener has 48 tulip bulbs to plant. If she plants 6 bulbs in each row, how many rows will she make?
follow_up_questions: The first 2 rows are by the gate. How many rows are not by the gate?
How many bulbs are planted in those rows?
Squirrels dig up 29 of those bulbs. How many bulbs are left in those rows?

problem: Every shelf in the toy shop holds 6 teddy bears. The shop has 48 teddy bears. How many shelves can it fill?
follow_up_questions: 2 of the shelves are by the window. How many filled shelves are elsewhere in the shop?
How many bears are on those other shelves?
Customers buy 29 of the bears from those shelves. How many bears are still on them?

problem: In two days, 34 families visited the zoo. If 19 came on Saturday, how many families came on Sunday?
follow_up_questions: Every family that came on Sunday had 3 members. How many people visited on Sunday?
17 of those visitors were children. How many were grown-ups?

problem: How many puppets did the puppet club make on Sunday? Over the whole weekend they made 34, and 19 of them were made on Saturday.
follow_up_questions: Every puppet made on Sunday has 3 buttons sewn on. How many buttons is that?
17 of those buttons are red. How many are not red?

problem: A teacher handed out 18 of her 25 stickers during the lesson. How many stickers did she have left?
follow_up_questions: Tomorrow she will get 20 more. How many stickers will she have then?

problem: The coach cut up 25 oranges for the soccer match. The players ate 18 of them at half-time. Find the number of oranges left.
follow_up_questions: For the next match he cuts 20 more oranges. How many oranges will he have for that match?

problem: Mr. Lindqvist bought 8 fish tanks for the classroom and 14 for the library. How many tanks did he buy in all?
follow_up_questions: He puts 3 goldfish in each tank. How many goldfish does he need?
He already has 40 goldfish. How many more must he buy?

problem: What is the number of picnic tables in the park if 8 are on the left side and 14 are on the right side?
follow_up_questions: Each table gets 3 jars of lemonade for the festival. How many jars are needed?
The volunteers have made 40 jars so far. How many more jars must they make?

problem: A pet shop has 9 cages, and 4 hamsters live in each cage. How many hamsters are in the shop?
follow_up_questions: Each hamster eats 2 carrots a day. How many carrots are needed each day?
Carrots come in bags of a dozen. How many bags are used each day?
A bag of carrots costs 5 dollars. How much do the carrots cost each day?

problem: Find the number of candles on the cakes: Grandpa Jonas ordered 9 small cakes for the family party, and each cake has 4 candles.
follow_up_questions: Every candle comes with 2 sugar stars. How many sugar stars are there?
The stars are packed in boxes of 12. How many boxes of stars is that?
One box of stars costs 5 dollars. What do all those boxes cost?

problem: A class of 27 students went on a field trip, and 19 of them wore raincoats. How many students did not wear raincoats?
follow_up_questions: Then 5 of the students without raincoats borrowed ponchos from the bus driver. How many students still have no rain cover?

problem: In the car park, 19 of the 27 cars are white. What number of cars are some other colour?
follow_up_questions: 5 of the cars that are not white drive off. How many cars of other colours are left?

problem: Aunt Sofia planted 20 sunflower seeds along the fence, and 14 of them sprouted. How many seeds did not sprout?
follow_up_questions: Her neighbour gives her 9 sunflower seedlings. How many sunflower plants does she have now?
Rabbits eat 2 of the plants. How many plants are left?

problem: How many balloons did not inflate properly? At the party, Lucas tried to blow up 20 balloons, but only 14 filled up nicely.
follow_up_questions: His mum brings 9 more blown-up balloons. How many good balloons are there now?
2 of them pop. What number of balloons is left?

problem: Zara took 12 cookies out of the jar for her friends, and 7 cookies were still in the jar. How many cookies were in the jar to begin with?
A bus driver counted 7 passengers left on her bus after 12 got off at the stadium. How many passengers were on the bus before the stadium stop?
The bouncy castle can be used for 12 sessions a day. If 9 sessions have already happened today, how many sessions are left?
follow_up_questions: Each session costs 4 dollars. How much money will the remaining sessions bring in?
How much money will all of today's sessions bring in?

problem: A boat at the lake may give 12 trips a day. It has already taken 9 trips today. What number of trips can it still make?
follow_up_questions: A trip costs 4 dollars. How much will the boat owner earn from the trips that are left?
What will the owner earn from all of today's trips together?

problem: Omar had 30 marbles. After a game at break time, he had 12. How many marbles did he lose?
follow_up_questions: He gives half of the marbles he has left to his little sister. How many marbles does she get?

problem: There are 12 beads left in Priya's box now, but there were 30 when she started making bracelets. How many beads did she use?
follow_up_questions: Half of the beads that are left go on a necklace. How many beads are on the necklace?

problem: Leah took 25 dollars to the book fair and came home with 9 dollars. How much did she spend?
follow_up_questions: Each book she bought cost 2 dollars. How many books did she buy?
She already had 47 books at home. How many books does she have now?
She puts them on shelves, 5 books on each shelf. How many shelves does she fill?

problem: At the end of the toy market, 9 dollars were left in Kai's pocket. He had gone there with 25 dollars. What did he spend?
follow_up_questions: Every toy car he bought cost 2 dollars. How many toy cars did he buy?
His collection already had 47 toy cars. How many cars does it have now?
He lines them up in rows of 5. How many rows does he make?

problem: Tomas built a tower of blocks 48 centimetres tall, but the cat knocked 13 centimetres off the top. How tall is the tower now?
follow_up_questions: He adds 9 centimetres of blocks. How tall is it then?
His sister's tower is twice as tall. How tall is her tower?

problem: A snowman in the yard was 48 centimetres tall. The sun came out and melted 13 centimetres away. What is its height now?
follow_up_questions: That night the children pack on 9 centimetres of fresh snow. How tall is the snowman now?
The snowman next door is twice that height. How tall is it?

problem: Hana had 20 dollars and bought a scarf for 13 dollars. How much money does she have left?
A toy robot cost Arjun 13 dollars. He had brought 20 dollars to the shop. How many dollars did he have after buying it?
The ice-cream van offers 14 flavours. By evening, 6 flavours have run out. How many flavours can children still choose? The van plays a cheerful tune.
follow_up_questions: The driver opens a freezer with 3 more flavours. How many flavours are on offer now?

problem: How many kinds of cake are still for sale? The school bake sale started with 14 kinds, and 6 were gone by noon. Parents had baked them the night before.
follow_up_questions: A teacher brings 3 more kinds from the staff room. How many kinds are for sale now?

problem: Mr. Haddad had 35 empty flower pots. After planting, 17 pots are still empty. How many pots did he plant flowers in?
follow_up_questions: He puts the planted pots on trays, 6 to a tray. How many trays does he fill?
Each tray sells for 30 dollars. How much money will he make from the trays?

problem: Aiko has 35 candle jars. 17 of them are still empty, and wax has been poured into the rest. How many candles has she made?
follow_up_questions: She packs the finished candles in gift boxes of 6. How many boxes does she fill?
She sells each gift box for 30 dollars. How much will she earn?

problem: A bakery sold 15 loaves of rye bread this morning and has 8 left. How many rye loaves did it bake?
With 8 kites still hanging in the shop window after 15 were sold, how many kites did the shop have at first?
The family ate 9 apples from the fruit bowl during the week, and now 6 are left. How many apples were in the bowl at the start of the week?
follow_up_questions: Dad wants 20 apples in the bowl for the weekend. How many must he add?

problem: How many chairs did the caretaker set out in the hall? After the meeting, 9 had been folded away and 6 were still standing.
follow_up_questions: For the concert she needs 20 chairs set out. How many more chairs must she set out?

problem: A flower seller sold 28 tulips at the market and has 16 left in her bucket. How many tulips did she bring?
follow_up_questions: Her friend brings her 9 more tulips. How many tulips does she have now?
She ties them into bunches of 5. How many bunches does she make?
Each bunch sells for 3 dollars. How much money will she get for all the bunches?

problem: Uncle Dario still has 16 lemons in his crate after selling 28 at the fruit stall. With how many lemons did he start?
follow_up_questions: His tree drops 9 more ripe lemons that afternoon. How many lemons does he have now?
He puts 5 lemons in each bag. How many bags can he fill?
A bag costs 3 dollars. What will he earn if he sells all the bags?

problem: Noor had 25 dollars and paid 8 dollars for a paint set. How much money does she have now?
follow_up_questions: Her aunt gives her 10 dollars. How much does she have now?
She buys 3 more paint sets at 8 dollars each. How much money is left?

problem: A pack of trading cards costs 8 dollars. Jonah, who had 25 dollars, bought one pack. What is left in his wallet?
follow_up_questions: He earns 10 dollars helping in the garden. How much does he have then?
Then he buys 3 more packs at 8 dollars each. What money remains?

problem: At the start of the month, the art room had 22 bottles of glue. By the end, only 9 were left. How many bottles were used?
follow_up_questions: A delivery brings 15 new bottles. How many bottles of glue are there now?

problem: How many bags of rice did the restaurant use, if it had 22 bags on Monday and 9 bags on Sunday night?
follow_up_questions: The supplier drops off 15 bags. What is the number of bags now?

problem: 45 runners started the school fun run, but 13 stopped before the finish. How many runners crossed the finish line?
A choir of 45 singers was set to perform, but 13 had colds and stayed home. What number of singers performed?
Mia had 19 crayons in her box, and she lost 5 of them at school. How many crayons are left in the box?
follow_up_questions: She buys 2 packs of 6 crayons. How many crayons will she have then?
She splits them equally between her 2 pencil cases. How many crayons go in each case?

problem: What number of sheep are on the farm now? There were 19 sheep, and 5 of them were sold at the fair.
follow_up_questions: The farmer buys 2 small flocks of 6 lambs each. How many animals does he have when they arrive?
He puts them into 2 fields, the same number in each. How many animals go in each field?

problem: Ella's piano concert was 21 days away when she started practising a new song. Now 8 days remain. For how many days has she practised? Her piano is painted white.
follow_up_questions: She practised the song 3 times on each of those days. How many times has she played it so far?

problem: The class trip is now 8 days away. When the children began saving coins for it, the trip was 21 days away. The trip is to a big science centre. How many days have they been saving?
follow_up_questions: They saved 3 coins every day. How many coins have they saved?

problem: Chloe gave 14 shells to her friend Hana and still has 23. How many shells did Chloe have at first?
follow_up_questions: Chloe finds 8 more shells on the beach. How many does she have now?
Hana now has twice as many shells as Chloe gave her. How many shells does Hana have?

problem: How many marbles did Pedro start with, if he now has 23 after handing 14 to his brother Luis?
follow_up_questions: Pedro wins 8 marbles in a game. How many marbles does he have now?
Luis now owns twice as many marbles as Pedro handed him. How many marbles does Luis own?

problem: The bike shop had 16 old bikes and sold 7 of them at the spring sale. How many old bikes are left?
A library gave away 7 of its 16 beanbags to a nursery school. What number of beanbags does the library still have?
A baker used 36 cups of flour for bread and has 18 cups left in the bin. How many cups of flour were in the bin before?
follow_up_questions: Each cake takes 6 cups of flour. How many cakes can she bake with the flour that is left?

problem: There are 18 sheets of coloured paper left in the art cupboard after the class used 36 sheets for lanterns. How many sheets were there before the lesson?
follow_up_questions: Each paper crown needs 6 sheets. How many crowns can be made with the sheets that are left?

problem: A new pencil was 20 centimetres long. After lots of sharpening it is 13 centimetres long. How much of it has been sharpened away?
follow_up_questions: The next week it loses another 8 centimetres. How long is it now?
A ruler is 3 times as long as that. How long is the ruler?

problem: How much soap did Malia use up? Her new bar of soap was 20 millimetres thick, and now it is 13 millimetres thick.
follow_up_questions: Another week of washing takes off 8 millimetres. How thick is it now?
Her sister's bar is 3 times as thick. How thick is her sister's bar?

problem: At the parade, Lucia handed out 13 flags. She still has 8 in her bag. How many flags did she have at the start?
follow_up_questions: The wind blows 2 flags out of her bag! How many are left in the bag?

problem: How many sandwiches did Coach Reyes pack, if he gave away 13 after the match and has 8 left in his cooler?
follow_up_questions: A dog grabs 2 sandwiches from the cooler. How many sandwiches remain?

problem: Leo baked 31 cookies and put 16 of them in a tin for the school fair. How many cookies are left for the family?
follow_up_questions: He shares them equally among 3 children, himself included. How many cookies does each child get?
His sister Rosa already had 7 cookies. How many does Rosa have now?
Rosa eats 4 of them. How many cookies does she have left?

problem: Of the 31 grapes Amira picked, 16 went into a fruit salad. How many grapes can she snack on?
follow_up_questions: She splits them equally among 3 friends, herself included. How many grapes does each friend get?
Her friend Dalia had 7 grapes already. How many grapes does Dalia have now?
Dalia eats 4. How many grapes does she have left?

problem: A farmer had 26 sacks of flour in the barn. After sending some to bakeries, 11 sacks are left. How many sacks did he send?
follow_up_questions: Each bakery got 5 sacks. How many bakeries got flour?
His mill grinds 9 more sacks next week. How many sacks will be in the barn then?

problem: What length of ribbon did the sewing club give to schools, if it had 26 metres and 11 metres are left?
follow_up_questions: Every school got 5 metres. How many schools got ribbon?
The club buys 9 more metres. How much ribbon will it have then?

problem: A gardener had 40 seed packets and gave 23 to the school garden club. How many packets does she have left?
There were 40 balloons at the start of the parade. Clowns handed out 23 of them to children. Find how many balloons the clowns still hold.
The lemonade stand made 36 cups this morning. At the end of the day, 9 cups were not sold. How many cups were sold?
follow_up_questions: Each cup sold for 2 dollars. How much money came in?
The lemons and sugar cost 19 dollars. How much money was made after paying for them?

problem: How many paper fans did the craft stall sell? It opened with 36 fans and closed with 9.
follow_up_questions: A fan costs 2 dollars. How much did the stall take for the fans it sold?
The paper for the fans cost 19 dollars. How much was left after paying for the paper?

problem: Ivan's ball of string was 45 metres long. After flying his kite, only 17 metres were left on the ball. How many metres of string did he lose? Kites filled the sky above the park.
A roll of wrapping paper held 45 metres. The gifts all had silver bows. Holiday gifts used up some of the paper, and 17 metres are still on the roll. How much paper went on the gifts?
A bookshop had 24 copies of a new comic. After the weekend, 5 copies were left. How many were sold?
follow_up_questions: Each copy cost 6 dollars. How much money did the shop take for them?

problem: How many hot dogs were sold at the game, if the vendor started with 24 and had 5 left at the final whistle?
follow_up_questions: One hot dog costs 6 dollars. What did the vendor earn?

problem: Kofi took 9 coins out of his piggy bank to buy a snack, and 16 coins are still inside. How many coins were in the piggy bank at first?
follow_up_questions: He spends those coins on the snack, and later his grandpa drops 12 new coins into the bank. How many coins are in the bank now?
If he sorts the coins into stacks of 4, how many stacks does he make?
He wraps 3 of the stacks in paper. How many coins are wrapped?

problem: There are 16 cards still in Elena's card box after she pulled out 9 to swap with friends. How many cards were in the box before?
follow_up_questions: She swaps the cards she pulled out for 12 new ones and adds those to the box. How many cards are in it now?
She sorts them into piles of 4. How many piles are there?
She puts 3 piles in a special folder. How many cards are in the folder?

problem: Mr. Nakamura has 27 pepper plants left after giving 18 to his neighbours. How many pepper plants did he grow?
follow_up_questions: He plants his own in rows of 9. How many rows does he plant?
Each row gives 20 peppers. How many peppers will he pick?

problem: A school grew strawberry plants for a sale. It sold 18 and kept 27 for its own garden. How many plants did it grow?
follow_up_questions: The kept plants go into beds of 9 plants each. How many beds are there?
If each bed produces 20 strawberries, how many strawberries will the school pick?

problem: The pool kiosk had 30 ice lollies in its freezer at noon. By closing time only 7 were left. How many lollies were sold?
follow_up_questions: An ice lolly costs 2 dollars. How much money did the kiosk take?

problem: A florist started the day with 30 roses and ended it with 7. What number of roses did she sell?
follow_up_questions: Each rose cost 2 dollars. How much money did she take in?

problem: Leo learned the words to 15 songs for the school concert. Now he can sing only 9 of them without a song sheet. How many songs has he forgotten?
How many of the class's 15 spelling words did Grace forget by Friday, if she still remembered 9?
Mrs. Patel bought 18 kilograms of rice for the school kitchen. The children ate 11 kilograms this week. How much rice is left?
follow_up_questions: She buys another 15 kilograms. How much rice is in the kitchen now?
If the kitchen uses 2 kilograms each day, how many days will the rice last?

problem: The horses on Aiden's farm munched 11 kilograms of carrots this weekend from a store of 18 kilograms. How many kilograms of carrots remain?
follow_up_questions: Aiden buys 15 kilograms more. What weight of carrots does he have now?
The horses eat 2 kilograms a day. For how many days will the carrots last?

problem: Ms. Kowalski put 32 cupcakes on the table. While she was out of the room, the puppy got to them. How many cupcakes did the puppy eat, if 19 were left?
follow_up_questions: She bakes 15 new cupcakes. How many cupcakes are there now?

problem: Only 19 of the 32 paper boats the children floated on the pond made it across. How many boats sank?
follow_up_questions: The children make 15 new boats. How many boats do they have now?

problem: Mrs. Ahmed had 23 goats on her farm and sold 8 of them at the market. How many goats does she have now?
follow_up_questions: Each goat eats 2 bundles of hay a day. How many bundles do the goats need each day?
A cartload of hay holds 90 bundles. For how many days will one cartload last?
She orders 4 cartloads. How many bundles of hay is that?

problem: A pet shop sold 8 of its 23 rabbits on Saturday. What number of rabbits does it still have?
follow_up_questions: Every rabbit gets 2 carrots a day. How many carrots does the shop need each day?
A crate holds 90 carrots. How many days will one crate last?
The shop buys 4 crates. How many carrots is that?

problem: Abdul packed 25 pencils for the school year. By winter he had lost or used up 9. How many pencils does he have left?
follow_up_questions: His mum gives him 6 more. How many pencils does he have now?

problem: The camping box held 25 batteries at the start of the trip. Torches and radios used up 9 of them. What number of batteries is left?
follow_up_questions: A friend lends them 6 more batteries. How many batteries do they have now?

problem: After the soccer match, 14 fans left right away and 12 stayed to meet the players. How many fans were there before anyone left?
follow_up_questions: Each fan who stayed got 2 photos with the players. How many photos were taken?
Three players posed for the photos, the same number each. How many photos did each player pose for?

problem: When story hour at the library ended, 12 children stayed to draw pictures and the other 14 went home. How many children had come?
follow_up_questions: Every child who stayed drew 2 pictures. How many pictures were drawn?
The pictures were hung on three walls, the same number on each. How many pictures are on each wall?

problem: Kemal baked 12 muffins and gave 5 to his neighbours. The muffins had blueberries in them. How many muffins did he keep?
How many paper cranes did Yuki keep? She folded 12 cranes and gave 5 to her classmates. Her favourite colour is purple.
Dad made 24 pancakes for the sleepover. In the morning 7 were still on the plate. How many pancakes did the children eat?
follow_up_questions: Dad eats 2 of the leftover pancakes. How many are left now?

problem: There were 24 slices of melon at the picnic, and 7 slices were still in the box afterwards. Find how many slices were eaten.
follow_up_questions: The dog sneaks 2 of the leftover slices. How many slices remain?

problem: A teacher had 21 pencil cases and has put pencils in 15 of them. How many cases are still empty?
follow_up_questions: She finds 4 more empty cases. How many empty cases are there now?
Each case needs 10 pencils. How many pencils does she need for the empty cases?

problem: How many flower boxes on the balcony have no plants yet, if Mr. Silva owns 21 boxes and has planted 15 of them?
follow_up_questions: He buys 4 more empty boxes. What number of empty boxes does he have now?
Each box needs 10 seeds. How many seeds does he need for the empty boxes?

problem: A parking lot has spaces for 60 cars, and 48 cars are already parked. How many more cars can park there?
follow_up_questions: Then a group of 15 cars arrives. If the lot fills up, how many of those cars must park somewhere else?

problem: The school bus can carry 60 children. 48 have already climbed aboard. What number of seats is still free?
follow_up_questions: A class of 15 children comes running up. Once the bus is full, how many of them will have to wait for the next bus?

problem: At the end of break, a teacher counts 68 children back inside the school. How many are still on the playground, if the school has 75 children?
follow_up_questions: She brings 4 of the playground children in. How many are still outside?
How many children are inside the school now?
If each classroom holds 8 children, how many classrooms are full?

problem: There are 75 sheep on Mr. Brennan's farm. At sunset, 68 of them are in the barn. How many sheep are still in the field?
follow_up_questions: The sheepdog brings 4 of them in. How many sheep are left in the field?
What number of sheep are in the barn now?
Each pen in the barn holds 8 sheep. How many pens are full?

problem: Ella went to the school shop with 85 cents and came out with 47 cents. How much did her notebook cost?
follow_up_questions: Then she buys 2 erasers for 15 cents each. How much money does she have left?
Her brother has three times as much money as she has left. How many cents does he have?

problem: A juice box at the fair took some of Omar's 85 cents. He had 47 cents after buying it. What did the juice box cost?
follow_up_questions: Next he buys 2 lollipops at 15 cents each. How many cents does he have left?
His cousin has three times as many cents as Omar has left. How many cents does his cousin have?

problem: The school stored 64 boxes of paper in the cupboard in September. Since then the teachers have used 47 boxes. How many boxes are left?
How many logs are left in the woodpile, if Grandpa stacked 64 logs in autumn and the fireplace has burned 47 of them?
The bakery had 58 kilograms of flour in its storeroom in the morning. After the bakers filled their mixing bowls, 19 kilograms were left. How much flour went into the bowls?
follow_up_questions: The bakers used 3 kilograms for each batch of bread. How many batches did they make?

problem: What weight of sand was moved to the sandpit? A pile of 58 kilograms of sand lay in the schoolyard, and after the children's shovelling only 19 kilograms remained.
follow_up_questions: They carried the sand in buckets of 3 kilograms each. How many buckets did they carry?

problem: A fish tank held 84 litres of water. While it was being cleaned, 47 litres were poured out. How much water is left in the tank?
follow_up_questions: Then 25 litres of fresh water are added. How much water is in the tank now?
The tank is full at 90 litres. How many more litres are needed to fill it?

problem: How much water is left in the garden barrel after the watering? It held 84 litres in the morning, and the children used 47 litres on the vegetable beds.
follow_up_questions: Rain adds 25 litres in the evening. How much water does the barrel hold now?
A full barrel holds 90 litres. How many litres short of full is it?

problem: A bag held 72 marbles at the start of break. The playground has a big oak tree. During break, the children lost 38 of the marbles in the grass. How many marbles were left in the bag?
How many stickers are still on the sheet? Ms. Rossi's sticker sheet had 72 stickers this morning, and her pupils earned 38 of them for good work. Her classroom is on the top floor.
Chef Amara took 23 potatoes out of the sack for soup. That left 45 potatoes in the sack. How many potatoes were in the sack before?
follow_up_questions: The next day she takes out 15 potatoes for chips. How many potatoes are in the sack now?

problem: 45 kilograms of birdseed remained in the zoo's store after the keeper used 23 kilograms to fill the feeders. What weight of birdseed was in the store at first?
follow_up_questions: The following morning he uses 15 kilograms more. How much birdseed is left in the store?

problem: When Sana got to the cinema, her film was due to start in 15 minutes. After buying popcorn, she had only 6 minutes left. How long did buying popcorn take?
follow_up_questions: Finding her seat took 4 minutes. How many minutes did she then wait for the film to start?
The film lasted 35 minutes. How many minutes passed from when she got to the cinema until the film ended?
Her friend arrived at the same moment but watched a shorter film and left 12 minutes sooner than Sana. How many minutes was her friend at the cinema?

problem: How long did Diego spend at the bakery? He walked out of his house when the school bus was due in 15 minutes, stopped at the bakery, and then had only 6 minutes left.
follow_up_questions: Walking from the bakery to the bus stop took 4 minutes. How long did he wait at the stop?
The bus ride to school took 35 minutes. How many minutes passed from leaving home to reaching school?
His sister left home at the same moment, rode her bike, and reached school 12 minutes sooner. How long did her trip take?

problem: A gardener had 45 metres of wire netting. After fencing the new vegetable bed, 17 metres were left. How much netting went around the bed?
follow_up_questions: The bed is square, and the netting went once around its 4 equal sides. How long is each side?

problem: What length of fairy lights went around the square patio? Grandma started with a 45-metre string, and 17 metres are left over.
follow_up_questions: The lights go exactly once around the patio's 4 equal sides. How long is one side?

problem: At the riding school, a stable hand gave the ponies 36 apples from a crate. Afterwards the crate still had 47 apples. How many apples were in the crate at the start?
How many grams of birdseed were in the jar before Ali filled the feeder? He poured 36 grams into the feeder, and 47 grams were left in the jar.
Before the picnic, Lena filled the cooler with 20 cans of juice. Everyone took cans, and afterwards 13 were left. How many cans were taken?
follow_up_questions: Then Lena gave 4 cans to the park ranger. How many cans are in the cooler now?
On the way home they buy twice as many cans as were taken at the picnic and put them in the cooler. How many cans does it hold after that?

problem: How many goldfish went into the classroom tank, if the school pond had 20 goldfish and 13 were left after the move?
follow_up_questions: Later 4 more goldfish from the pond were given to another school. How many goldfish are in the pond now?
In spring, the pond gets twice as many new goldfish as went into the tank. How many goldfish are in the pond after that?

problem: Mrs. Diaz printed 9 pages for her class, and the printer tray then had 47 sheets of paper. How many sheets were in the tray before she printed?
follow_up_questions: Later she prints 12 more pages. How many sheets are left in the tray?

problem: How many cupcakes were in the bakery window at opening time? After 9 were sold, 47 were still there.
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon 12 more are sold. How many cupcakes are left in the window?

problem: A delivery truck stopped at the first shop and dropped off 38 boxes. There were still 26 boxes on the truck. How many boxes did it carry at the start?
follow_up_questions: At the second shop it drops off 19 more boxes. How many boxes are on the truck now?
Then the driver picks up 3 stacks of 15 boxes each. How many boxes are on the truck now?
How many fewer boxes is that than at the very start?

problem: What was the number of passengers on the ferry when it set out? At the first island 38 people got off, and 26 stayed on board.
follow_up_questions: At the second island 19 more got off. How many people are still on the ferry?
Then 3 tour groups of 15 people each come aboard. How many passengers are on the ferry now?
How many fewer passengers is that than when the ferry set out?

problem: It takes Mateo 23 minutes to walk to his grandma's house, but only 9 minutes by bike. His bike has a shiny bell. How much time does biking save?
follow_up_questions: He bikes to her house 3 times this week. How many minutes of biking is that?

problem: How many minutes faster is the express train? The slow train takes 23 minutes to reach the city, and the express takes only 9 minutes. Both trains are painted red.
follow_up_questions: Ms. Lee rides the express 3 times. How many minutes does she spend on it?

problem: An apple tree in the yard had 52 apples. After the family picked some, only 4 were still on the tree. How many apples did the family pick?
follow_up_questions: They share the picked apples equally among 6 cousins. How many apples does each cousin get?
Each apple is cut into 5 slices. How many slices does one cousin get?

problem: Only 4 of the 52 cookies on the plate were left after the class party. Find how many cookies the children ate.
follow_up_questions: The eaten cookies were shared equally among 6 children. How many did each child eat?
Each cookie had 5 chocolate chips. How many chips did one child eat?

problem: Ahmed's paper plane flew 19 metres, while his sister's flew only 14 metres. How much farther did Ahmed's plane fly?
A red ribbon is 14 centimetres long and a blue ribbon is 19 centimetres long. What is the difference in their lengths?
A teacher sent 14 children out to the playground. That left 35 children in the hall. How many children were in the hall before?
follow_up_questions: Later, 9 more children from the hall go outside. How many are still in the hall?

problem: How many puppies were at the shelter before 14 were adopted, if 35 are still there?
follow_up_questions: Over the weekend, 9 more of them find homes. How many puppies are still at the shelter?

problem: A cargo ship arrived at the port with 74 containers. Cranes lifted 38 of them onto the dock. How many containers are still on the ship?
follow_up_questions: The containers left on the ship are stacked evenly in 4 rows. How many are in each row?
One row is unloaded at the next port. How many containers stay on the ship?

problem: What number of books is still in the delivery van? It reached the school with 74 books, and the librarian carried 38 inside.
follow_up_questions: The rest are split evenly into 4 crates. How many books go in each crate?
One crate is dropped off at the next school. How many books are still in the van?

problem: Aunt Rosa baked 12 pies for the village fair. When the fair closed, 9 pies were still on the table. How many pies did people buy?
follow_up_questions: Each pie was cut into 4 slices. How many slices were sold?

problem: How many litres of soup did the campers eat? The cook made 12 litres and had 9 litres left after dinner.
follow_up_questions: Each litre fills 4 bowls. How many bowls of soup were eaten?

problem: A hill path has 64 stone steps up to the castle gate. Jonas has climbed 37 of them. How many steps does he still have to climb?
follow_up_questions: Coming back down, he stops after 25 steps to tie his shoe. How many steps are still below him?
Each step is 15 centimetres high. How high above the bottom of the path is the castle gate?
A flag on the gate's arch is another 35 centimetres up. How high is the flag above the bottom of the path?

problem: Priya has climbed 37 steps on her way to the top floor of her apartment block. How many steps are left, if the stairs have 64 steps in all?
follow_up_questions: Going back down, she stops after 25 steps to chat with a neighbour. How many steps are below her now?
Every step is 15 centimetres high. How high is the top floor above the ground?
A window ledge is another 35 centimetres above the top step. How high is the ledge above the ground?

problem: A train left the city with 53 passengers. After the first station, the conductor counted 29. How many passengers got off at the first station?
53 children were at the swimming pool at noon. By lunchtime only 29 were still swimming. Work out how many children had gone home.
The classroom had 27 computers. A few were taken away for repair, and now 23 are left. How many computers were taken for repair?
follow_up_questions: Repairing one computer takes 6 days. How many days of repair work is that altogether?

problem: How many bikes from the school rack went to the repair shop? There were 27 bikes in the rack, and only 23 are there now.
follow_up_questions: Fixing one bike takes 6 hours. How many hours of work is that in total?

problem: Before the winter, Uncle Bo's big dog weighed 95 pounds. The dog loves chasing balls. After a long illness, it weighed 78 pounds. How many pounds did the dog lose?
follow_up_questions: Then it gains 6 pounds a week for 3 weeks. How much does it weigh then?
How many pounds heavier is it now than before the winter?

problem: What weight did the old seal at the aquarium lose? In spring it weighed 95 kilograms, and after a busy summer of swimming in the big pool it weighed 78 kilograms. It is the aquarium's favourite animal.
follow_up_questions: In autumn it gains 6 kilograms a week for 3 weeks. What does it weigh then?
How many kilograms heavier is it now than in spring?

problem: Sofia had 35 dollars when she arrived at the bowling alley. After paying for a game, she had 22 dollars. How much did the game cost?
How much did the concert ticket cost, if Liam had 35 dollars before buying it and 22 dollars after?
The school banner was 75 centimetres long, but Ali cut off 48 centimetres to make a sign. How long is the rest of the banner?
follow_up_questions: He cuts the rest into strips 3 centimetres wide. How many strips does he get?

problem: How long is the piece of licorice rope that is left? It was 75 centimetres long, and the friends ate 48 centimetres of it at the sleepover.
follow_up_questions: The leftover piece is cut into bits 3 centimetres long. How many bits is that?

problem: Farmer Chen sold 8 apple trees to a neighbour and kept the other 34 for his own orchard. How many apple trees had he grown?
follow_up_questions: He plants the trees he kept in 2 equal rows. How many trees go in each row?
Each tree needs 3 buckets of water a week. How many buckets does one row need each week?
One week the rain gives the row as much as 20 buckets. How many buckets must he carry that week?

problem: How many pumpkin plants did Mrs. Akande raise? She kept 34 for her own garden and gave 8 to the school.
follow_up_questions: She plants hers in 2 rows with the same number in each. How many plants are in each row?
Each plant needs 3 litres of water a week. How many litres does one row need each week?
Rain gives that row 20 litres one week. How many litres must she add with the hose?

problem: On Monday Aiko skipped rope 64 times without stopping. On Tuesday she managed 49. How many fewer skips did she do on Tuesday?
follow_up_questions: On Wednesday she did 12 more skips than on Tuesday. How many skips did she do on Wednesday?
How many skips did she do on Tuesday and Wednesday together?

problem: How many fewer push-ups did Coach Mendes do on Tuesday than on Monday? He did 64 on Monday and 49 on Tuesday.
follow_up_questions: On Wednesday he did 12 more than on Tuesday. What was Wednesday's count?
What is the total for Tuesday and Wednesday?

problem: During the day, a leaky paddling pool lost 17 litres of water. By evening it held 46 litres. How much water was in it in the morning?
follow_up_questions: Overnight another 30 litres leak out. How much water is left?

problem: How much water was in the rain barrel at noon, if 17 litres evaporated in the afternoon sun and 46 litres were left by evening?
follow_up_questions: Overnight the gardener uses 30 litres on the roses. How much water remains?

problem: Volunteers carried 26 boxes of food from the storeroom to the hall. There were still 57 boxes in the storeroom. How many boxes were in the storeroom before?
57 bricks were still in the pile after the builders used 26 to build a garden wall. Find the number of bricks in the pile at first.
The school play had 41 seats left to sell on the last day. When the box office closed, 38 were still unsold. How many seats were sold on the last day?
follow_up_questions: Each seat cost 4 dollars. How much money was taken that day?
The money buys juice boxes at 2 dollars each. How many juice boxes can be bought?

problem: How many melons did the farm stall sell, if it had 41 melons in the morning and 38 were left unsold at closing?
follow_up_questions: Each melon sold for 4 dollars. How much did the stall make?
The farmer spends that money on seed packets at 2 dollars each. How many packets can he buy?

problem: A ball of yarn had 60 metres. Grandma used 52 metres to knit a scarf. How much yarn is left?
follow_up_questions: A hat needs 15 metres of yarn. How many more metres does she need to buy?

problem: What length of fabric is left on the bolt? The tailor started with 60 metres and cut 52 metres for curtains.
follow_up_questions: Tablecloths for the cafe need 15 metres. How many more metres must the tailor buy?

problem: At the start of the week, the school kitchen had 85 kilograms of flour. The kitchen has a big silver oven. By Friday only 39 kilograms were left. How much flour was used that week?
follow_up_questions: The next week the kitchen used 8 kilograms less. How much flour did it use then?
How much flour was used over the two weeks?
The cook orders 99 kilograms for the next two weeks. If the kitchen uses the same amount as before, how many kilograms will be left over?

problem: How much paint did the painters use this week? On Monday there were 85 litres of paint in the store, and by Saturday only 39 litres were left. The workers wear white overalls.
follow_up_questions: The following week they used 8 litres less. How many litres did they use then?
What is the total amount used over the two weeks?
The boss buys 99 litres for the next two weeks. If they use the same total as before, how many litres will be spare?

problem: The pet shop had 50 bags of dog food. On sale day, 46 bags were sold. How many bags are left?
follow_up_questions: A delivery brings 35 more bags. How many bags does the shop have now?

problem: How many chairs are still in the storeroom? It held 50 chairs, and the caretaker carried 46 into the hall for the concert.
follow_up_questions: The school borrows 35 chairs from the church and puts them in the storeroom. How many chairs are in the storeroom now?

problem: A spool on Grandma's sewing machine held 70 metres of thread. After sewing curtains, she had used 64 metres. How much thread is left on the spool?
follow_up_questions: She winds on another 45 metres. How much thread is on the spool now?
She uses 17 metres to hem a skirt. How much thread is still on the spool?

problem: What length of string is left on Nadia's kite reel? It held 70 metres, but a gust snapped the string and her kite flew off with 64 metres of it.
follow_up_questions: She winds on a new piece of string 45 metres long. How much string is on the reel now?
She lets out 17 metres to fly her new kite. How much string is still on the reel?

problem: A painter filled a large can with 25 litres of paint and used 20 litres on the garage door. How much paint is left in the can?
How many litres of water are left in the dogs' water barrel? It held 25 litres, and 20 litres went into their bowls this week.
Pablo cut 3 centimetres off a ribbon to tie a bow. The ribbon is now 27 centimetres long. How long was it before?
follow_up_questions: His pencil is 18 centimetres long. How much longer is the ribbon than the pencil?

problem: The tug-of-war rope is 27 metres long now, after the coach cut off a frayed end of 3 metres. What was its length before?
follow_up_questions: The gym is 18 metres wide. How much longer is the rope than the gym is wide?

problem: The stable's oat bin held 90 kilograms at sunrise. At sunset 34 kilograms were left. How many kilograms of oats did the horses eat today?
follow_up_questions: The oats were given in 4 equal feeds. How many kilograms were in each feed?
Tomorrow there will be 5 such feeds. How many kilograms of oats will be needed?
How much more is that than what is left in the bin?

problem: How much birdseed did the bird park use today? Its seed barrel had 90 kilograms in the morning and 34 kilograms by evening.
follow_up_questions: The seed was put out in 4 equal portions. How many kilograms were in each portion?
Tomorrow the keepers plan 5 such portions. How many kilograms will they need?
How many kilograms more is that than what remains in the barrel?

problem: Mr. Okafor scooped 5 kilograms of rice into a pot for the festival, which left 95 kilograms in the storage bin. How much rice was in the bin first?
follow_up_questions: He packs the rice from the bin into 5-kilogram bags. How many bags does he fill?
He sells each bag for 3 dollars. How much money does he get?

problem: 95 litres of juice were still in the factory tank after a worker filled a 5-litre jug for a taste test. How many litres were in the tank before?
follow_up_questions: The juice in the tank is poured into 5-litre bottles. How many bottles are filled?
Each bottle sells for 3 dollars. How much money will the bottles bring in?

problem: A pump at the bike shop could fill 60 tyres before it needed recharging. At closing time, it had enough air left for only 14. How many tyres were filled that day?
follow_up_questions: Half of those tyres belonged to children's bikes. How many tyres were on children's bikes?

problem: Jaya's bag of clay was enough to make 60 small pots. Now there is only enough left for 14. How many pots has she made?
follow_up_questions: Half of them cracked in the kiln. How many pots did not crack?

problem: During practice, the swim team swam 4 lengths of freestyle, then 9 lengths of backstroke, and finally 6 more lengths of freestyle. How many lengths did they swim?
follow_up_questions: The other swim team swam 25 lengths. How many more lengths was that?
How many lengths did the two teams swim together?

problem: How many songs did the band play at the fair? They began with 4 slow songs, played 9 dance songs, and ended with 6 more slow songs.
follow_up_questions: The band before them played 25 songs. How many more songs did that band play?
How many songs did both bands play altogether?

problem: Aliyah read 3 pages of her book before breakfast. Her book has a red cover. During the morning she read 12 more pages, and after lunch another 5. How many pages did she read that day?
follow_up_questions: Each page has 25 lines. How many lines did she read during the morning alone?

problem: How many laps of the track did Jun run on sports day? He jogged 3 laps to warm up, ran 12 laps in the big race, and cooled down with 5 more. The sun shone all afternoon.
follow_up_questions: Each race lap took him 25 seconds. How many seconds did the race take?

problem: The school kitchen made 6 litres of tomato soup, 3 litres of pea soup and 9 litres of carrot soup. How many litres of soup did it make?
follow_up_questions: The soup is poured into pots that hold 2 litres each. How many pots are filled?
The teachers take 7 pots to the staff room. How many pots are left?

problem: What is the total number of paint pots on the art shelf, if there are 6 yellow, 3 purple and 9 orange?
follow_up_questions: The pots are put into trays of 2. How many trays are needed?
The art class borrows 7 trays. How many trays are left on the shelf?

problem: The pet shop has 5 parrots, 11 budgies and 3 canaries. How many birds does it have altogether?
Find the total number of trucks in Theo's toy box: 3 fire trucks, 5 dump trucks and 11 tow trucks.
By Wednesday, Mrs. Garcia's class had planted 4 trees this week. They planted 7 more on Thursday and 3 more on Friday. How many trees have they planted this week?
follow_up_questions: Their goal is 20 trees. How many more trees do they need to plant?

problem: How many books has Kirra read this month? She had read 4 by the middle of the month, then finished 7 more the next week and 3 more in the last week.
follow_up_questions: Her goal for the month is 20 books. How many more must she read?

problem: At the doctor's office, Amira spent 4 minutes signing in, 7 minutes in the waiting room and 4 minutes being weighed. How long did all that take?
follow_up_questions: The doctor saw her 6 minutes later. How long had she been at the office by then?
Getting home took 3 times as long as that. How long did getting home take?
Her brother's trip home was 18 minutes shorter. How many minutes did it take?

problem: How many minutes did Felix spend getting ready for school? He spent 4 minutes brushing his teeth, 7 minutes eating breakfast and 4 minutes putting on his shoes.
follow_up_questions: Then he waited 6 minutes for his friend. How many minutes passed in all?
His bus ride to school took 3 times as long as that. How long was the ride?
His friend's ride was 18 minutes shorter. How long did his friend ride?

problem: Maria's family plans a drive to the beach: 32 kilometres to the first town, 28 kilometres to the next, then 85 kilometres to the coast. How long is the whole drive?
follow_up_questions: So far they have driven 60 kilometres. How far do they still have to go?
Their friends have 15 fewer kilometres left to drive. How far do the friends still have to go?

problem: How many stickers will Ben have stuck in once he fills all three of his sticker books? The first book has room for 32, the second for 28 and the third for 85.
follow_up_questions: So far he has stuck in 60 stickers. How many more does he need?
His friend Mina needs 15 fewer than that. How many does Mina need?

problem: At the post office, Mrs. Kim mailed three parcels: one weighing 6 kilograms, one weighing 19 kilograms and one weighing 14 kilograms. There were 5 people in the queue ahead of her. What do the parcels weigh together?
follow_up_questions: The post office lets one customer send 45 kilograms a day. How many more kilograms could she send?

problem: What is the total weight of the Tanaka family's shopping? They carried 6 kilograms of fruit, 19 kilograms of potatoes and 14 kilograms of flour back from 5 market stalls.
follow_up_questions: Their car's boot can hold 45 kilograms. How many more kilograms could it take?

problem: At the class bake sale, Hamza baked 6 pies, Lily baked 13 and Tom baked 8. How many pies were baked altogether?
The Tigers scored 13 goals in the school tournament, the Eagles 6 and the Sharks 8. What was the total number of goals?
The class fish tank had 7 fish. On Monday the teacher added 5 goldfish, and on Friday she added 5 guppies. How many fish are in the tank now?
follow_up_questions: Each fish eats 5 food flakes a day. How many flakes do all the fish eat in a day?
The food tin has 99 flakes. How many are left after one day?

problem: How many ducks live on the farm pond now? There were 7 ducks, then Grandma Ilse bought 5 white ducks in spring and 5 brown ducks in summer.
follow_up_questions: Each duck eats 5 handfuls of grain a day. How many handfuls do they eat each day?
The grain sack holds 99 handfuls. How many handfuls are left after one day?

problem: A snail crawled 6 metres on Monday. It crawled 8 metres on Tuesday and 5 metres on Wednesday. What distance did it crawl in those three days?
follow_up_questions: The garden wall is 33 metres from where it started. How far does it still have to go?
It covers the rest in 2 days, crawling the same distance each day. How far does it crawl each day?
Each metre takes it 15 minutes. How many minutes does it crawl on each of those days?

problem: How far did Amina paddle her canoe over three days? On day one she paddled 6 kilometres, then 8 kilometres, then 5 kilometres.
follow_up_questions: The river route is 33 kilometres long. How much of it is left?
She finishes it in 2 more days, paddling equal distances. How far does she paddle each day?
Each kilometre takes her 15 minutes. How many minutes does she paddle on each of those days?

problem: The class vegetable bed had 4 tomato plants. On Tuesday the children planted 9 more, and on Saturday a parent brought 6 more. The bed is next to the gym. How many tomato plants are in the bed now?
follow_up_questions: The teacher moves 7 plants into a sunnier bed. How many plants stay?
The ones that stay share the bed with 3 times as many onion plants. How many onion plants are there?

problem: How many rabbits live at the petting farm now? It started the year with 4 rabbits, got 9 more in March and another 6 in June. Visitors love to feed them carrots.
follow_up_questions: 7 rabbits move to a farm school. How many stay?
The rabbits that stay live with 3 times as many guinea pigs. How many guinea pigs are there?

problem: For the class trip, 3 children chose the museum, 14 chose the zoo and 6 chose the park. How many children chose a trip?
How many children are in the art club, if 14 of them like painting best, 6 like clay best and 3 like drawing best?
The Ito family's savings jar had 8 dollars in it at the start of April. They added 15 dollars that month and 27 dollars in May. How much is in the jar now?
follow_up_questions: Their neighbours' jar has 12 dollars less. How much is in the neighbours' jar?

problem: How tall is the snow pile by the school gate now? It was 8 centimetres high on Monday, then 15 centimetres of snow fell on Tuesday and 27 centimetres more on Wednesday.
follow_up_questions: The pile by the back door is 12 centimetres lower. How high is that pile?

problem: The school's music teacher tuned 18 guitars, 24 violins and 9 cellos before the concert. How many instruments did she tune?
follow_up_questions: Each instrument took her 3 minutes. How long did the tuning take?
She also took a 20-minute tea break. How many minutes passed from start to finish?

problem: How many cars did the car wash clean on Saturday, if it washed 18 cars in the morning, 24 in the afternoon and 9 in the evening?
follow_up_questions: Every car took 3 minutes to dry. How many minutes of drying was that?
Add the 20 minutes it took to clean the machines. How many minutes is that altogether?

problem: Kwabena practised his piano piece 7 times before school, 12 times after school and 7 times before bed. How many times did he practise it that day?
follow_up_questions: His teacher wants 64 practice runs before the concert. How many are still to go?

problem: How many pages of her puzzle book did Lucia finish on the road trip? She did 7 pages in the car, 12 pages at the hotel and 7 more pages on the drive home.
follow_up_questions: The puzzle book has 64 pages. How many pages are still unfinished?

problem: In the garden, Pavel used 4 metres of string to tie up the beans, 16 metres to mark out the vegetable beds and 4 metres to hang a bird feeder. How much string did he use?
follow_up_questions: His ball of string had 50 metres. How much string is left?
He cuts the leftover string into 2 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
He ties one piece to a 9-metre piece from his neighbour. How long is the joined string?

problem: How many metres of fabric did the costume club use? They needed 4 metres for a cape, 16 metres for the stage curtains and 4 metres for a flag.
follow_up_questions: The club had a 50-metre bolt of fabric. How much is left?
The leftover fabric is cut into 2 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
One piece is sewn to a 9-metre piece given by a parent. How long is the sewn piece?

problem: At the fair, Sven spent 12 minutes on the carousel, 25 minutes at the games and 18 minutes eating candy floss. How long was he at the fair?
follow_up_questions: His cousin stayed 20 minutes longer than he did. How long did his cousin stay?
How many minutes did the two of them spend at the fair altogether?

problem: How long did Ms. Haruka's swimming lesson last, if she spent 12 minutes warming up, 25 minutes on strokes and 18 minutes on games?
follow_up_questions: The advanced lesson lasts 20 minutes longer. How long is the advanced lesson?
What is the total time of both lessons?

problem: Pia's backpack holds 4 notebooks, 9 markers and 13 crayons. How many things are in her backpack?
Find the total number of toys on the nursery shelf: there are 13 blocks, 4 dolls and 9 toy cars.
To mark out a race track, the coach laid 6 metres of white rope, 14 metres of blue rope and 9 metres of orange rope. How much rope did he lay?
follow_up_questions: He had bought a 40-metre bundle. How many metres are left?
A parent gives him a 23-metre rope to add to the leftovers. How many metres does he have for next time?

problem: What length of fairy lights did Ravi hang on the balcony? He hung 6 metres along the railing, 14 metres around the door and 9 metres over the window.
follow_up_questions: His string of lights was 40 metres long. How many metres are left over?
His sister adds her own 23-metre string to the leftovers. How many metres do they have for next year?

problem: On Saturday, Elif read 14 pages of her book in the morning and 6 more in the afternoon. Her friend Rana read 17 pages that day. How many pages did the two girls read altogether?
follow_up_questions: On Sunday they read 9 pages fewer in total. How many pages did they read on Sunday?
Each page has 25 lines. How many lines did they read on Sunday?

problem: How many lengths of the boating pond did two brothers row on Saturday? Musa rowed 14 lengths in the morning and 6 in the afternoon, while Idris rowed 17.
follow_up_questions: On Sunday their total was 9 lengths lower. How many lengths did they row on Sunday?
Each length of the boating pond is 25 metres. How many metres did they row on Sunday?

problem: In the school garden challenge, Ana planted 3 seedlings in March, 7 in April and 12 in May. She wrote each plant's name on a little stick. How many seedlings did she plant?
follow_up_questions: She gave each seedling 30 drops of plant food. How many drops did she use?

problem: How many puzzles did Mateo finish in the puzzle club? He finished 3 in October, 7 in November and 12 in December. His favourite one showed a lighthouse.
follow_up_questions: Each puzzle had 30 pieces. How many pieces did he put together?

problem: Abdi's sacks of potatoes weigh 9 kilograms, 12 kilograms and 15 kilograms. How heavy are the three sacks together?
The class made three paper chains for the hall. Joined end to end, how long are they, if one is 9 metres, one is 12 metres and one is 15 metres long?
At the zoo, Keanu walked 45 steps to the lion house, 32 steps to the penguins and 45 steps back to the gate. How many steps did he take?
follow_up_questions: His little brother took 2 steps for every one of his. How many steps did his brother take?
Then the family walked 58 more steps to the car park. How many steps did Keanu take in total?
His mum took 30 fewer steps than Keanu in total. How many steps did she take?

problem: Count the metres Dalia swam: 45 metres out to the raft, 32 metres around it and 45 metres back to the beach.
follow_up_questions: Her older cousin swam twice as far as Dalia did. How many metres did her cousin swim?
Later Dalia swam 58 metres more along the shore. How far did she swim in total?
Her friend swam 30 metres less than Dalia's total. How far did her friend swim?

problem: Before lunch, the ice-cream truck sold 8 cones, 17 cups and 8 ice lollies. How many treats did it sell?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon it sold 3 times as many ice lollies as before lunch. How many ice lollies did it sell in the afternoon?
How many ice lollies did it sell that day altogether?

problem: What is the number of items the garden centre sold this morning, if it sold 8 rose bushes, 17 bags of soil and 8 watering cans?
follow_up_questions: This afternoon it sold three times as many watering cans as this morning. How many watering cans did it sell this afternoon?
How many watering cans were sold over the whole day?

problem: In the chess club this year, Ingrid won 9 games, lost 5 and drew 4. How many games did she play?
follow_up_questions: Each game lasted 40 minutes. How many minutes did she spend playing?
Next year she plans to play 6 more games than this year. How many games is that?
This year each win was worth 3 points and each draw 1 point. How many points did she score?

problem: How many matches did the hockey team play this season? They won 9, drew 4 and lost 5.
follow_up_questions: A match lasts 40 minutes. How many minutes did they play this season?
Next season has 6 more matches than this one. How many matches is that?
This season a win earned 3 points and a draw earned 1 point. How many points did the team earn?

problem: Over three weeks, Haruto built model planes: 4 in the first week, 4 in the second and 11 in the third. How many model planes did he build?
The woodwork club built 11 birdhouses in its third month. In the first month it built 4, and in the second month another 4. How many birdhouses has it built?
For the school picnic, Sana brought 5 packs of juice and Diego brought 8. The teacher already had 12 packs in her bag. How many packs of juice do they have?
follow_up_questions: Each pack has 3 juice boxes. How many juice boxes is that?
There are 68 children at the picnic, and each gets one juice box. How many juice boxes are left over?

problem: How many pizzas are there for the team party? There were already 12 in the kitchen, the coach ordered 5 more, and a parent brought 8.
follow_up_questions: Each pizza feeds 3 guests. How many guests can be fed?
68 guests come to the party. How many extra servings are there?

problem: On its first trip, the ferry picked up 6 people at the north dock, 6 at the south dock and 15 at the island. How many people got on altogether?
follow_up_questions: At the harbour 19 of them got off. How many people are still on the ferry?

problem: How many children climbed into the school minibus? 6 got in at the farm, 6 at the bridge and 15 in the village.
follow_up_questions: At school, 19 of them hopped out first. How many are still in the minibus?

problem: For the new reading corner, the school ordered 5 beanbags, 18 cushions and 5 rugs. The corner will be painted yellow. How many items did the school order?
follow_up_questions: They are shared equally among 4 classrooms. How many items go to each classroom?
Each item costs 8 dollars to clean. How much does it cost to clean one classroom's items?

problem: How many plants did the garden club order for the courtyard? It ordered 5 lemon trees, 18 herb pots and 5 rose bushes. The courtyard gets lots of sun.
follow_up_questions: The plants are shared equally among 4 flower beds. How many go in each bed?
Each plant needs 8 litres of soil. How many litres of soil does one bed need at least?

problem: In the dressing-up chest there are 3 pairs of boots, 12 pairs of gloves and 5 pairs of earrings. What is the number of pairs in the chest?
follow_up_questions: A pair of earrings is two earrings. How many single earrings are in the chest?

problem: How many pairs of shoes are in the school shoe rack, if there are 5 pairs of sandals, 3 pairs of boots and 12 pairs of trainers?
follow_up_questions: Each pair of sandals is 2 sandals. How many single sandals are on the rack?

problem: Hoang caught 27 fish at the lake and his aunt caught 38. They gave 46 fish to the village kitchen. How many fish did they keep?
follow_up_questions: A neighbour gave them 17 more fish. How many fish do they have now?

problem: How many leaflets are still waiting to be delivered? Two volunteers printed 27 and 38 leaflets, and 46 have already gone into letterboxes.
follow_up_questions: The office prints 17 more. How many leaflets are waiting now?

problem: A toy shop had 16 teddy bears and 9 toy rabbits. This week 12 of these toys were sold. How many are left?
The school orchestra had 16 violin players and 9 flute players, but 12 of them moved up to the senior orchestra this term. What number of players are left?
A kite shop received 8 kites on Monday and 7 on Tuesday, but 3 had torn sails and were returned. How many kites are on display?
follow_up_questions: Each hook on the wall holds 4 kites. How many hooks are full?
Each hook needs 80 centimetres of wall. How much wall space do those hooks need?

problem: What number of jars of jam did Gran put in the pantry? She made 8 jars on Saturday and 7 on Sunday, and 3 cracked and were thrown away.
follow_up_questions: Each pantry shelf fits 4 jars. How many shelves are filled?
Every shelf is 80 centimetres wide. How wide are those shelves added together?

problem: A cafe had 36 plates on the shelves and 48 in the cupboard. At lunchtime, customers used 59 of them. How many clean plates are left?
follow_up_questions: The dishwasher returns 30 clean plates. How many clean plates are there now?

problem: How many sheets of paper are still unused? The art room had 36 sheets on the table and 48 in the drawer, and the children used 59 for their paintings.
follow_up_questions: The teacher brings 30 new sheets. How many unused sheets are there now?

problem: Oliver drew 28 pictures at home and 19 at art club. He threw away 16 he did not like. How many drawings did he keep?
follow_up_questions: He picks 15 of them for the school art show. How many drawings are not in the show?
Each drawing in the show is 9 centimetres wide. If they hang side by side, how wide is the row?
The display board is 14 centimetres wider than the row. How wide is the board?

problem: How many seashells did Noa have after sorting? She found 28 on Monday and 19 on Tuesday, and then threw 16 broken ones back into the sea.
follow_up_questions: She glues 15 of them onto a picture frame. How many are not on the frame?
Each shell on the frame is 9 millimetres wide. Laid in a line, how long is the row of shells?
The frame is 14 millimetres longer than the row. How long is the frame?

problem: The school hall has 4 doors. To decorate it, Mr. Dube unrolled 35 metres of paper chain from one box and 35 metres from another. He hung 28 metres along the stage. How many metres of paper chain does he have for the rest of the hall?
follow_up_questions: The rest of the hall has 3 walls that each need the same length of chain. How many metres go on each wall?

problem: How many metres of rope are left for the climbing frame? The playground team cut 35 metres from one coil and 35 metres from a second coil, and used 28 metres for the rope bridge. There are 4 swings in the playground.
follow_up_questions: The rest is shared equally among 3 climbing nets. How many metres does each net get?

problem: Jamal caught 21 tadpoles in the pond and his teacher caught 14. Only 26 of them fit in the class tank. How many tadpoles had to go back to the pond?
How many of the pumpkins were too small for carving? The farmer grew 21 in one field and 14 in another, and 26 were big enough.
A shelter took in 28 cats in January and 36 in February. Families adopted 41 of them. How many cats are still at the shelter?
follow_up_questions: In March, 15 more cats arrive. How many cats are at the shelter now?
The cats are split equally between 2 rooms. How many cats are in each room?

problem: How many library books are still out on loan? Readers borrowed 28 books in March and 36 in April, and 41 have been returned.
follow_up_questions: In May, 15 more books are borrowed. How many books are out on loan now?
All of them are held by 2 school classes, the same number each. How many books does each class have?

problem: The two rain barrels in the garden held 34 litres and 45 litres. During the dry week Grandma used 62 litres on her plants. How much water was left in the barrels?
follow_up_questions: A storm on Sunday adds 25 litres. How much water do the barrels hold now?

problem: How much milk was left in the two churns? One held 34 litres and the other 45 litres, and the dairy sold 62 litres at the market.
follow_up_questions: On Monday the farmer adds 25 litres of fresh milk. How much milk do the churns hold now?

problem: The rival team in the school quiz finished with 55 points. Laila's team earned 27 points in round one and 31 in round two. What was the size of Laila's winning lead?
follow_up_questions: In their next quiz they scored 9 more points than in this one. How many points was that?
How many points did they score in the two quizzes together?

problem: The Blue class collected 27 cans in the first week of the food drive and 31 in the second, while the Red class collected 55 in all. How many more cans did the Blue class collect?
follow_up_questions: The next month Blue collected 9 more cans than its total this time. How many cans was that?
How many cans did Blue collect in the two months together?

problem: Ms. Ortiz planned 25 minutes of reading and 35 minutes of maths for the afternoon. The classroom has a big map on the wall. A fire drill stopped the lessons after 48 minutes. How many minutes of lessons were missed?

How many minutes of the concert did the audience miss? The band planned to play for 25 minutes before the break and 35 minutes after it, but a power cut ended the show after 48 minutes. The stage lights were purple.
A juice bar squeezed 9 litres of orange juice in the morning and 14 litres in the afternoon. Customers drank 14 litres. How much juice was left?
follow_up_questions: The leftover juice is shared equally among 3 jugs. How many litres go into each jug?

problem: How much soup was left over at the school kitchen? The cooks made 9 litres for the first lunch and 14 litres for the second, and the children ate 14 litres.
follow_up_questions: The leftover soup goes into 3 pots, the same amount in each. How many litres are in each pot?

problem: Tariq earned 18 dollars selling lemonade and got 25 dollars from his grandparents. He spent 16 dollars on a football. How much money does he have left?
follow_up_questions: He wants a skateboard that costs 35 dollars. How much more does he need?
He earns 2 dollars each time he washes his uncle's car. How many car washes does he need?
Each wash takes 15 minutes. How many minutes of washing is that?

problem: How much money is left in Anya's purse? She had 18 dollars of pocket money, her aunt gave her 25 dollars, and she paid 16 dollars for a book.
follow_up_questions: A pair of skates costs 35 dollars. How much more money does she need for them?
She gets 2 dollars each time she waters the neighbour's garden. How many times must she water it?
Watering takes 15 minutes each time. How many minutes will she spend watering?

problem: On Saturday the bakery baked 34 loaves of white bread and 27 loaves of brown bread. At closing time 18 loaves were left. How many loaves did customers buy?
follow_up_questions: On Sunday they sold 6 loaves more than on Saturday. How many loaves did they sell on Sunday?
How many loaves were sold over the whole weekend?

problem: How many tickets were sold for Saturday's puppet show? The theatre printed 34 tickets for the morning show and 27 for the afternoon show, and 18 were left unsold.
follow_up_questions: Sunday's shows sold 6 more tickets than Saturday's. How many tickets were sold on Sunday?
How many tickets were sold over the weekend?

problem: The painters mixed 45 litres of blue paint in one drum and 38 litres in another. They used 66 litres on the school fence. How much paint is still in the drums?
follow_up_questions: They mix 30 more litres. How much paint is in the drums now?

problem: How much lemonade is left for sports day? The cooks made 45 litres in one tub and 38 litres in another, and the runners drank 66 litres.
follow_up_questions: The cooks make 30 more litres. How much lemonade is there now?

problem: 19 girls and 24 boys signed up for the cooking class, but the kitchen has room for just 15. How many children will have to wait for the next class?
How many campers will not get a canoe? The camp has 15 canoe places, and 24 boys and 19 girls want to paddle.
A river boat set off with 26 tourists and collected 17 more at the bridge. At the castle, 35 tourists went ashore. How many stayed on the boat?
follow_up_questions: At the market pier, 14 people came aboard. How many passengers are on the boat now?
The boat has 48 seats. How many seats are empty?

problem: How many children were left in the swimming pool? There were 26 at the start of the session, 17 more jumped in later, and then 35 climbed out for lunch.
follow_up_questions: After lunch 14 children jump back in. How many are in the pool now?
The pool allows 48 swimmers at a time. How many more children could get in?

problem: A party host bought 24 red balloons and 18 gold ones. Each of the 29 guests took one balloon home. How many balloons were left?
follow_up_questions: Each balloon cost 40 cents. What did the leftover balloons cost?

problem: How many pencils were left after each of the 29 pupils took one? The teacher had 24 red pencils and 18 blue pencils in the pot.
follow_up_questions: Each pencil costs 40 cents. What are the leftover pencils worth?

problem: A gardener poured 25 litres of water into a big tub and then added 19 more. She used 31 litres to water the flower beds. How much water is left in the tub?
follow_up_questions: She adds 40 litres before watering the lawn. How much water does the tub hold now?
The lawn takes 28 litres. How much is left after that?
She pours the rest into 5 watering cans, the same amount in each. How many litres go into each can?

problem: How many litres of fuel are left in the tractor? Farmer Joy put in 25 litres in the morning and 19 litres at noon, then used 31 litres ploughing.
follow_up_questions: She adds 40 litres before mowing the hay field. How much fuel is in the tank now?
Mowing uses 28 litres. How much fuel is left?
She drains what is left into 5 cans, with the same amount in each. How many litres go into each can?

problem: The snow on the mountain path was 58 centimetres deep. Another 7 centimetres fell overnight, and then the sun melted 19 centimetres. How deep is the snow now?
How tall is Arjun's tower of cups now? It was 58 centimetres high, he added 7 centimetres more, and then his cat knocked 19 centimetres off the top.
